                    ### Question
                    An investigator studying targeted therapy in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors requires a reliable test to determine the spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells in biopsy specimens. Which of the following is the most appropriate test?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Flow cytometry
opb. Immunohistochemistry
opc. Western blot
opd. Northern blot
ope. Fluorescence in-situ hybridization

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Immunohistochemistry is the most appropriate test for determining the spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells in biopsy specimens as it can detect the CD117 antigen. This is supported by the fact that CD117-positive cells express the CD117 antigen. Fluorescence in-situ hybridization, although capable of detecting genetic alterations, is not the most suitable test for spatial distribution in this context.
